summary: Iteration 6 validates the closed-system RBAC + brute-force lockout + audit log work for D1 Custódia. Backend: 20/20 pytest cases passed (test_rbac_iter6.py) covering closed registration (403), generic 401, lockout 423 after 5 fails, success clears counter, /api/users CRUD with admin/operator + region/password validations, soft-delete, self-deactivation guard, inactive-login 401, operator custody RBAC (own region 200, other 403, PATCH other-region 403), audit log listing + admin-only + filter. Frontend: admin dashboard shows Usuários + Auditoria menu items; operator nav hides them and /usuarios + /auditoria redirect to /dashboard; region-locked element is rendered with Guarulhos label; bad login → 401 red banner; lockout → 423 amber/yellow banner with the lockout message; user-management dialog creates a user via UI (POST /users → 201); login footer reads 'Sistema fechado · Solicite acesso ao administrador.' (no register link).

minor.issue: When changing role to 'operator' WITHOUT providing region in the same payload, the endpoint does NOT enforce that the user has a region. Region is only validated when data.region is present (line 1181). Result: a user could become operator with a stale/null region. Recommend validating after merging fields: if final role==operator and (current_region or new_region) not in VALID_REGIONS → 400.

ui_bugs.issue: Console warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined} for {DialogContent}'. Add a <DialogDescription> for accessibility.

action_items: (Optional/Minor) Tighten PATCH /api/users/{id} region validation: when final role is 'operator', the merged region must be in VALID_REGIONS regardless of whether 'region' was sent in the patch body.
(Optional/Minor) Add DialogDescription to the 'New/Edit User' dialog to silence the radix accessibility warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1374 lines — should be split (auth.py / users.py / audit.py / custodies.py / exports.py). This was already flagged in iter5 but has only grown.

PATCH /users region validation is partial (see backend.minor): the rule 'operator must have region' is only enforced when client sends region in the patch body; missing path 'role:operator-only patch' lets a user become operator without re-validating existing region.
POST /users always returns 201 even for first-time admin creation, while in audit logs we record 'user_created' with role/region. Consider also auditing failed creation attempts (currently silent).
/api/audit-logs has no max cap on 'limit' param — a caller could request limit=100000. Add an upper bound (e.g., min(limit, 500)).

/auth/login generic message is good, but response also leaks state: a successful login returns is_active=true while inactive users get a generic 401. That is correct, but record_login_attempt() is called even on invalid email — which means the brute-force lockout works on emails that don't exist (correct/desired). Confirmed via test.

seed_data_creation: Created several TEST_* users during pytest — all are deactivated by tests' cleanup or by post-run sweep. Two TEST_ui_* users created via UI smoke were also cleaned up via DELETE /api/users.
context_for_next_testing_agent: RBAC + closed system + lockout + audit log all verified end-to-end. operador.gru@d1.com is preserved active for future iterations. The brute-force test strategy uses unique random emails so it never locks real accounts. Login UI styles: red = 401 generic ('Acesso não autorizado...'), amber/yellow = 423 lockout. /register route always lands on /login.
rca of the issue: N/A — no critical bugs found. One minor logical gap in PATCH /users role-change region validation noted as action item.
